title: Asia's Largest Clay Buddha Is 34.5m Long | Qinghai-Gansu Loop EP6 | China Travel Expert
description:
Stop six on the Qinghai-Gansu loop hides a giant most travelers drive right past: Asia's largest reclining Buddha made of clay, 34.5 meters long.

Zhangye's Great Buddha Temple (Dafo Si) in Gansu was built in 1098 during the Western Xia dynasty, and it's the largest and best-preserved Western Xia imperial temple still standing. The reclining Buddha inside runs 34.5m from head to foot, with shoulders 7.5m across, ears about 4m long and feet over 5m — one ear is taller than a grown adult. It was built over a hidden wooden armature, then modeled in clay and straw and gilded. After the temple, the reward on this leg of the drive is a bowl of hand-pulled Gansu noodles.

🧭 Expert Tip: Photography is not allowed inside the Buddha hall — put the camera away and stand near the statue's feet, where the full 34.5m scale finally hits you.
